US corporate AI spending hit a new high in October 2026, but growth was modest.

The Ramp AI Index, which tracks AI spending among business customers of financial services provider Ramp, showed a 1.65 percent increase month over month.

The heaviest AI users spent somewhat more, according to Ramp. The top one percent of companies by AI spending paid a median of $10,200 per employee per month, up nine percent. A typical company, by contrast, spent just $16.32, a slight increase of less than a dollar from the previous month.

Ramp's data reflects market trends but isn't necessarily representative. The index draws on payment data from more than 85,000 US companies, though free AI tools and usage through personal accounts may be missing from the figures.

According to Ramp, separate metrics on token volume and spending come only from companies using Ramp Token Spend Management and aren't representative of overall AI spending on the platform. The customer base skews growth-oriented, tech-savvy, and larger than US businesses overall, so AI adoption is likely overstated.

OpenAI's spending grows faster than Anthropic's

Business customers' spending on OpenAI grew 2.1 percent month over month, compared with just 0.5 percent for Anthropic. According to Ramp chief economist Ara Kharazian, the structural risks he identified in his earlier analysis persist. One percent of companies drive 80 percent of revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic.

That top tier is mostly venture-backed firms in tech, finance, and technical services. Outside those sectors, AI adoption is barely spreading.

Prices are falling at the same time. The average price per million processed text tokens dropped 21 percent last month, according to Ramp. Usage volume is growing faster than spending, so AI keeps getting cheaper, driven by competitive pressure between OpenAI and Anthropic along with open-weight models from China.

Source: Ramp Rate

SpacexSI also grew strongly at 2.2 percent, making it the fastest-growing software company in Ramp's entire dataset. That likely says more about bias in Ramp's data than about any big win for Grok. The company's models aren't particularly noteworthy, and the growth is probably driven by the coding tool Cursor, which belongs to SpacexSI. On Ramp, the company holds a 6.3 percent market share, a figure that most likely doesn't reflect the broader market. Anthropic reached 44.8 percent adoption, up 1.1 percentage points, while OpenAI held steady at 40.6 percent. Overall adoption of AI services rose to 56.8 percent.

Customer support gains ground as a growth driver

Software development teams accounted for 72 percent of all tracked AI spending in October, but their spending has declined from summer highs. Customer support and customer success departments saw the strongest growth, with their share of AI spending climbing from 0.8 percent in June to 13.3 percent in October, possibly driven by AI chatbots in customer service. Leadership teams also spent slightly more.

Source: Ramp Rate

But customer support is nowhere near matching the rapid growth development teams posted earlier this year, Kharazian writes. These use cases also tend to favor cheaper, faster models over the most expensive flagship ones.

For OpenAI and Anthropic, that means new customers may bring lower margins. The share of the most expensive models, which Kharazian identifies as Opus, Fable, Sol, and Astra, still edged up slightly in October, reaching 69.5 percent of total spending.

translation.html:
2026年10月，美国企业的AI支出创下新高，但增长幅度不大。

Ramp AI指数追踪金融服务提供商Ramp的企业客户的AI支出，该指数显示，支出环比增长1.65%。

据Ramp称，AI使用量最大的企业支出有所增加。按AI支出排名前1%的企业，每名员工每月支出的中位数为10,200美元，增长9%。相比之下，一家典型企业每名员工每月仅支出16.32美元，比上个月小幅增加，不足1美元。

Ramp的数据反映了市场趋势，但未必具有代表性。该指数采用了超过85,000家美国企业的支付数据，不过，免费AI工具以及通过个人账户使用AI的情况可能未被计入。

据Ramp称，有关token用量和支出的单独指标仅来自使用Ramp Token Spend Management的企业，不能代表该平台整体的AI支出情况。与美国企业的总体情况相比，Ramp的客户群更偏向注重增长、熟悉技术且规模较大的企业，因此数据很可能高估了AI的采用程度。

OpenAI相关支出的增长快于Anthropic

企业客户在OpenAI上的支出环比增长2.1%，而在Anthropic上的支出仅增长0.5%。据Ramp首席经济学家Ara Kharazian称，他在此前分析中指出的结构性风险依然存在。1%的企业贡献了OpenAI和Anthropic收入的80%。

这些头部企业大多来自科技、金融和技术服务行业，并获得了风险投资支持。在这些行业之外，AI的采用几乎没有扩大。

与此同时，价格也在下降。据Ramp称，上个月，每处理100万个文本token的平均价格下降了21%。使用量的增长快于支出的增长，因此AI的使用成本持续下降，推动因素包括OpenAI与Anthropic之间的竞争压力，以及来自中国的开放权重模型。

来源：Ramp Rate

SpacexSI也实现了2.2%的强劲增长，成为Ramp整个数据集中增长最快的软件公司。这很可能更多地反映了Ramp数据的偏差，而非Grok取得了什么重大胜利。该公司的模型并没有特别突出的表现，增长很可能由隶属于SpacexSI的编程工具Cursor推动。在Ramp平台上，该公司的市场份额为6.3%，这一数字很可能无法反映更广泛的市场情况。Anthropic的采用率达到44.8%，上升1.1个百分点，而OpenAI保持在40.6%。AI服务的整体采用率升至56.8%。

客户支持作为增长动力的作用增强

10月，软件开发团队占所有受追踪AI支出的72%，但其支出已从夏季高点回落。客户支持和客户成功部门的增长最为强劲，其AI支出占比从6月的0.8%攀升至10月的13.3%，这可能是由客服场景中的AI聊天机器人推动的。管理团队的支出也略有增加。

来源：Ramp Rate

但Kharazian写道，客户支持的增长远未达到开发团队今年早些时候的快速增长水平。这些应用场景也往往更青睐价格更低、速度更快的模型，而非最昂贵的旗舰模型。

对于OpenAI和Anthropic而言，这意味着新客户带来的利润率可能更低。Kharazian所指的最昂贵模型包括Opus、Fable、Sol和Astra，这些模型的支出占比在10月仍略有上升，达到总支出的69.5%。
